subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The development of nuclear weapons after 1945 changed warfare chiefly by introducing what?
options: The threat of mass destruction and deterrence
questions.explain: Nuclear weapons created the threat of mass destruction and the strategy of deterrence in the Cold War.

questions.q: What was the main feature of fighting on the WWI Western Front?
options: Static trench warfare with little movement
questions.explain: The Western Front settled into a deadlocked line of trenches where attacks gained little ground.

questions.q: During the Crimean War (1853-56), failings in which area shocked the British public?
options: The care of sick and wounded soldiers
questions.explain: Reports of squalid hospitals and neglected wounded, highlighted by Nightingale, caused public outrage.

questions.q: How did the Industrial Revolution most change 19th-century warfare?
options: It allowed mass production of weapons and use of railways and the telegraph
It made cavalry the dominant force again
It ended the use of all firearms
It removed governments from war planning
questions.explain: Industry mass-produced weapons while railways, steamships and the telegraph transformed logistics.

questions.q: In the Napoleonic era, the British army was recruited mainly by which method?
options: Voluntary enlistment, often of the poor
questions.explain: Before conscription, Britain relied on volunteers, frequently drawn from the poorest in society.

questions.q: The term 'total war' in WWII refers to what?
options: The mobilisation of a country's entire society and economy for the war
A war with no rules or treaties
A war declared on every nation at once
A war fought only with new technology
questions.explain: Total war drew civilians, industry and resources fully into the war effort.

questions.q: Which new armoured weapon was first used by the British at the Somme in 1916?
questions.explain: Britain introduced the tank in 1916 to break the deadlock of trench warfare.

questions.q: The introduction of gunpowder weapons in late medieval warfare most reduced the importance of which traditional force?
questions.explain: Firearms and cannon could pierce armour, eventually making the armoured knight obsolete.

questions.q: The Blitz of 1940-41 was an example of which feature of modern warfare?
options: The bombing of civilian targets from the air
questions.explain: German aircraft bombed British cities, bringing the war directly to civilians on the home front.

questions.q: Conscription (compulsory military service) was first introduced in Britain during which conflict?
questions.explain: Britain introduced conscription in 1916 during WWI as volunteer numbers fell.

questions.q: During WWI and WWII, the 'home front' refers to what?
options: Civilian life and effort within Britain during the war
The front nearest to home soil in Europe
The naval defence of the coast
questions.explain: The home front covered civilian work, rationing and morale that supported the fighting forces.

questions.q: At the Battle of Crecy (1346) and Agincourt (1415), which English weapon proved decisive?
questions.explain: English and Welsh longbowmen devastated French forces at Crecy and Agincourt.
